sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: A major new poll from The Times finds that Vice President Kamala Harris has transformed the 2024 presidential race and is now leading President Trump
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一项重要新民调显示，副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯已经改变了2024年的总统竞选格局，目前在

sentences.en: in three of the most crucial battleground states.
sentences.zh: 三个最关键的摇摆州领先于特朗普总统。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Nate Cohn explains why Harris is benefiting so much from being a new face in an election that so many Americans had dreaded.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事内特·科恩将解释为什么哈里斯作为一张新面孔，能从许多美国人早已厌倦的这场选举中获得如此大的优势。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, August 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月13日，星期二。

sentences.en: Nate, The Times has just completed our first poll that seeks to understand the state of this presidential race since Biden dropped out and Kamala Harris took his place
sentences.zh: 内特，《纽约时报》刚刚完成了自拜登退选、卡玛拉·哈里斯接替他

sentences.en: as the Democratic nominee.
sentences.zh: 成为民主党候选人以来，旨在了解总统竞选现状的首份民调。

sentences.en: Everyone understands that that has changed this race.
sentences.zh: 大家都明白这改变了竞选态势。

sentences.en: But this poll attempted to measure by just how much it changed the race in three of the most essential swing states.
sentences.zh: 但这份民调试图衡量在三个最重要的摇摆州中，这种改变到底有多大。

sentences.en: So tell us about the results.
sentences.zh: 那么，请告诉我们结果吧。

sentences.en: Well, we found that the entry of Kamala Harris into the race has fundamentally upended this conteSt.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，卡玛拉·哈里斯的参选从根本上颠覆了这场竞争。

sentences.en: We polled Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, arguably the three most important battleground states.
sentences.zh: 我们调查了密歇根州、宾夕法尼亚州和威斯康星州，这可以说是三个最重要的战场州。

sentences.en: These are three states that voted for Obama in 2012,
sentences.zh: 这三个州在2012年投票给了奥巴马，

sentences.en: Trump in 2016, and then flip back to Biden in 2020.
sentences.zh: 2016年投给了特朗普，然后在2020年又转回支持拜登。

sentences.en: But that Trump had generally been leading in in the polling so far this cycle.
sentences.zh: 但在本轮竞选的民调中，特朗普此前一直处于领先地位。

sentences.en: And if Kamala Harris won all three states, she would almost certainly win the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 如果卡玛拉·哈里斯赢下这三个州，她几乎肯定会赢得总统大选。

sentences.en: And the poll found Harris leading Donald Trump in all three states by a four-point margin, 50 to 46 percent.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，哈里斯在这三个州均以50%对46%的优势领先唐纳德·特朗普，领先幅度为四个百分点。

sentences.en: A huge swing in favor of the Democrats in a very short period of time.
sentences.zh: 在很短的时间内，民主党获得了巨大的优势转变。

sentences.en: Basically, what this poll found was that she was a game-changer in those three states.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这份民调发现她在这些州是一个改变游戏规则的人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it is worth saying it's all on the Harris side of things.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，这完全归功于哈里斯一方。

sentences.en: Donald Trump's ratings are essentially unchanged since the last time he polled these states.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的支持率自上次民调以来基本没有变化。

sentences.en: In fact, his favorability rating ticked up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的好感度还略有上升。

sentences.en: But by replacing Joe Biden, who was really unpopular, with Kamala Harris, who in this poll is viewed favorably by 49 or 50 percent of voters
sentences.zh: 但通过用卡玛拉·哈里斯取代非常不受欢迎的乔·拜登，而哈里斯在这份民调中获得了49%到50%选民的好感，

sentences.en: in every state, they have completely changed what had been the basic dynamic of this election.
sentences.zh: 在每个州，他们彻底改变了这场选举的基本态势。

sentences.en: Until now, voters had been agonizing between two candidates they didn't like.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，选民们一直在两个他们都不喜欢的候选人之间纠结。

sentences.en: And we don't know what would have happened if we had played the Biden-Trump matchup to the end.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道如果拜登与特朗普的对决持续到最后会发生什么。

sentences.en: But we do know that, as of July, when voters were choosing between those two unpalatable options, more of them were choosing Trump.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，截至7月，当选民必须在两个令人不满的选择中做决定时，更多人选择了特朗普。

sentences.en: Now they don't have to.
sentences.zh: 现在他们不必这样了。

sentences.en: At least for now, they like Harris more than they like Trump.
sentences.zh: 至少目前看来，他们比喜欢特朗普更喜欢哈里斯。

sentences.en: And so she has the lead.
sentences.zh: 所以她取得了领先。

sentences.en: So let's talk about who has rallied around Harris once Biden got out of the race and how that helps explain why she's suddenly in the lead in these three states.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们谈谈在拜登退选后，谁聚集到了哈里斯身边，以及这如何解释她为何突然在这三个州取得领先。

sentences.en: Harris' biggest gains are coming from the demographic groups that traditionally vote Democratic, but that Joe Biden had struggled to consolidate throughout much of the year.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯最大的增长来自于传统上支持民主党，但乔·拜登在今年大部分时间里难以整合的人群。

sentences.en: Take Black voters.
sentences.zh: 以黑人选民为例。

sentences.en: The poll finds her up 81 to 13 among Black voters across these three states.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，在这三个州，她在黑人选民中的支持率以81%比13%领先。

sentences.en: That's a lot better than Biden had been in polls this year.
sentences.zh: 这比拜登今年在民调中的表现要好得多。

sentences.en: I mean, we had done some polls that found Joe Biden in the 60s among Black voters at times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之前做过一些民调，发现乔·拜登在黑人选民中的支持率有时仅在60%左右。

sentences.en: That feels really important, Nate, because Black voters are a group that helped power Biden to victory in 2020 in states like Georgia.
sentences.zh: 内特，这感觉非常重要，因为黑人选民是帮助拜登在2020年赢得佐治亚州等州的关键群体。

sentences.en: It's a group of voters that Trump has been very heavily focused on and one of the groups that appeared most open to defecting from the Democratic side
sentences.zh: 这是特朗普一直非常关注的选民群体，也是最有可能因为特朗普而从民主党阵营

sentences.en: to the Republican side because of Trump.
sentences.zh: 倒戈到共和党阵营的群体之一。

sentences.en: So those kinds of gains feel very meaningful.
sentences.zh: 所以这些增长感觉非常有意义。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And another group that sort of has those same characteristics as young voters, the poll found Harris ahead by 15 points among 18 to 29-year-olds in these three states.
sentences.zh: 另一个具有类似特征的群体是年轻选民，民调显示哈里斯在这三个州的18至29岁选民中领先15个百分点。

sentences.en: It's not the best number of Democrats that ever produced among young voters, to be frank, but it's a lot better than Joe Biden for much of the year.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这并不是民主党在年轻选民中取得过的最好成绩，但比乔·拜登今年大部分时间的表现要好得多。

sentences.en: And these are two groups where it's easy to see why she would do a little bit better than Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 这两个群体很容易看出她为什么会比乔·拜登表现得更好。

sentences.en: She's much younger than he is.
sentences.zh: 她比他年轻得多。

sentences.en: She's Black.
sentences.zh: 她是黑人。

sentences.en: He's white.
sentences.zh: 他是白人。

sentences.en: She's also a woman, and it's worth noting that she's doing better among women than Joe Biden had been doing in our previous surveys.
sentences.zh: 她也是女性，值得注意的是，她在女性选民中的表现比乔·拜登在我们之前的调查中要好。

sentences.en: What's maybe more surprising, though, is she's still at least holding her own among older voters, among men, among white voters.
sentences.zh: 不过，也许更令人惊讶的是，她在老年选民、男性选民和白人选民中依然保持着自己的优势。

sentences.en: She's not doing better than Biden was in these polls, but she's not doing worse.
sentences.zh: 她在这些民调中的表现并不比拜登更好，但也没有更差。

sentences.en: So she's adding a lot of strength among traditionally Democratic constituencies without giving up much, if any, ground among the groups that you might expect
sentences.zh: 所以她在传统民主党选民群体中增加了很大的优势，同时在那些你可能认为

sentences.en: to be relative weak points for her.
sentences.zh: 是她相对弱点的群体中，也没有丢失多少阵地。

sentences.en: You said that a lot of this seemingly across-the-board improvement in the numbers for Harris seems to be driven by the fact that both Trump and Biden
sentences.zh: 你说哈里斯在数据上看似全面的提升，似乎很大程度上是因为特朗普和拜登

sentences.en: are not especially popular candidates.
sentences.zh: 都不是特别受欢迎的候选人。

sentences.en: And, of course, now Biden's out of the race.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在拜登已经退出了竞选。

sentences.en: So I guess my question is, how much are Harris's gains reflective not just of
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我的问题是，哈里斯的增长在多大程度上反映了

sentences.en: Biden or Trump's problems, but of her own popularity?
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是拜登或特朗普的问题，而是她自身的受欢迎程度？

sentences.en: It's definitely a reflection of her own popularity and standing.
sentences.zh: 这绝对反映了她自身的受欢迎程度和地位。

sentences.en: On every question that we asked, people say that they like Harris.
sentences.zh: 在我们提出的每一个问题上，人们都说他们喜欢哈里斯。

sentences.en: They say she's intelligent.
sentences.zh: 他们说她很聪明。

sentences.en: They say she's honeSt.
sentences.zh: 他们说她很诚实。

sentences.en: They say she cares about you.
sentences.zh: 他们说她关心你。

sentences.en: I think the more interesting question is, why?
sentences.zh: 我认为更有趣的问题是，为什么？

sentences.en: I mean, just as recently as a few weeks ago, a majority of Americans said they had an unfavorable view of Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就在几周前，大多数美国人还表示他们对卡玛拉·哈里斯持负面看法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I even came on the show and we talked about all of her different political liabilities and challenges and how bad her 2019 campaign was.
sentences.zh: 我甚至上过节目，我们讨论了她所有的政治包袱和挑战，以及她2019年的竞选有多糟糕。

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们确实讨论过。

sentences.en: And now all of a sudden,
sentences.zh: 而现在突然之间，

sentences.en: Kamala Harris is broadly liked and popular.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯广受喜爱和欢迎。

sentences.en: And it's happened extremely quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且发生得非常快。

sentences.en: And I think that there are really a mix of two basic reasons that this can happen.
sentences.zh: 我认为这背后有两个基本原因的混合。

sentences.en: One is that she's really changed people's views about them because she's made this brand new impression with the help of great media coverage.
sentences.zh: 一是她确实改变了人们对她的看法，因为在出色的媒体报道帮助下，她留下了全新的印象。

sentences.en: Or she's benefiting from this new contrast, this comparison with Joe Biden and the burst of pent-up
sentences.zh: 或者她正受益于这种新的对比，即与乔·拜登的比较，以及人们长期以来

sentences.en: Democratic energy from people who have been yearning for something different.
sentences.zh: 对改变的渴望所积压的民主党能量的爆发。

sentences.en: I think it's probably a little bit of both.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I mean, I was just explaining to a friend recently that it's sort of like the country just had a breakup with Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我最近刚向一位朋友解释，这就像这个国家刚刚和乔·拜登分手了。

sentences.en: They've been in this relationship for years that they weren't happy with and maybe they didn't even know how unhappy they were with this relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们维持这段关系多年，却并不快乐，甚至可能都没意识到自己在这段关系中有多不快乐。

sentences.en: But now that they've had this breakup, they're newly liberated.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们分手了，他们感到了一种新的解放。

sentences.en: There's this incredible sense of new opportunity and now comes along
sentences.zh: 有一种不可思议的新机遇感，现在卡玛拉·哈里斯出现了，

sentences.en: Kamala Harris and after their first few dates with Kamala, the country is thrilled.
sentences.zh: 在与卡玛拉的最初几次约会后，这个国家感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: This is quite a metaphor and to indulge it a little bit further, when such a date between Americans and Kamala Harris was hypothetical because she wasn't the nominee
sentences.zh: 这真是一个绝妙的比喻，再深入一点说，当美国人和卡玛拉·哈里斯之间的这种约会还只是假设时，因为她不是候选人，

sentences.en: when she was just vice president, voters' views of her were less generous.
sentences.zh: 当她只是副总统时，选民对她的看法就不那么慷慨了。

sentences.en: But once this breakup with Biden happens, all that pent-up desire for change, that feeling of liberation you just mentioned, it overwhelms any previous doubts a lot of voters had
sentences.zh: 但一旦与拜登分手，那种对改变的积压渴望，那种你刚才提到的解放感，就压倒了许多选民之前对她

sentences.en: about her.
sentences.zh: 的任何疑虑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, we'll find out whether this is real and whether the country is going to marry her in a few months.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，几个月后我们会知道这是否真实，以及这个国家是否会与她“结婚”。

sentences.en: But for the moment, I think that Harris is enjoying this really coveted place in American politics where voters are able to invest most of their hopes and their wishes
sentences.zh: 但目前，我认为哈里斯正在享受美国政治中这个令人垂涎的位置，选民们能够将他们对候选人的大部分希望和愿望

sentences.en: for what they want to see in a candidate in this new figure.
sentences.zh: 都寄托在这个新人物身上。

sentences.en: You know, in polling, it's a little bit like something called a generic candidate or a generic Democrat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在民调中，这有点像所谓的“通用候选人”或“通用民主党人”。

sentences.en: Can you just explain that?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it might sound a little insulting to compare Kamala Harris to a generic Democrat, but it's really not.
sentences.zh: 是的，将卡玛拉·哈里斯比作一个“通用民主党人”听起来可能有点侮辱人，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: In a poll, a pollster might ask, would you rather vote for the Democrat or Donald Trump?
sentences.zh: 在民调中，民调专家可能会问，你更愿意投票给民主党人还是唐纳德·特朗普？

sentences.en: The Democrat is unnamed, not a real person.
sentences.zh: 这个“民主党人”是未具名的，不是一个真实的人。

sentences.en: And the unnamed generic candidate, and this is true for both parties, almost always fares better than a named candidate.
sentences.zh: 而未具名的通用候选人——这对两党都适用——几乎总是比具名的候选人表现得更好。

sentences.en: And that's because they're not burdened with all of the real world imperfections that actual real candidates have.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们没有背负真实候选人所具有的所有现实世界的不完美之处。

sentences.en: And I think that's sort of what's happened for Kamala Harris over the last few weeks is she's running as a broadly appealing mainstream Democratic candidate, and there are a bunch
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是过去几周卡玛拉·哈里斯身上发生的事情，她作为一名广受欢迎的主流民主党候选人参选，人们对她有很多好感，而且她还没有被以任何方式定义。

sentences.en: of good feelings around her, and she hasn't really been defined either way.
sentences.zh: 因此，选民们现在正将他们支持除唐纳德·特朗普之外的人的希望，寄托在他们对她的想象中，这给了她明显的领先优势。

sentences.en: And so voters are piling their hopes to support someone other than Donald Trump into their idea of her right now, and it's giving her a clear lead.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该把卡玛拉·哈里斯看作——特别是在一场她突然成为惊喜替代者的短期选举背景下——

sentences.en: So we should think of Kamala Harris, especially in the context of a very short election in which she's suddenly the surprise replacement
sentences.zh: 基本上是当下民主党人的柏拉图式理想，在某种真实意义上，她确实占据了你刚才描述的“通用民主党人”的位置。

sentences.en: Democratic nominee, as basically the platonic ideal of a Democrat in this moment who almost in a real sense does occupy that spot you just described of the generic Democrat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不寻常的位置，尽管“通用”这个词听起来可能不好，但它听起来是一个相当理想的位置。

sentences.en: It's an unusual position, and even though the word generic might sound bad, it sounds like a pretty ideal one.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，这也是她过去几周竞选的方式。

sentences.en: It is, and that's how she's been running her campaign for the last few weeks.
sentences.zh: 很高兴回来。

sentences.en: It's so good to be back.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 如果你看她的竞选演讲，就能看出来。

sentences.en: And you can see that if you watch her stump speech.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，我们正在目睹一场对来之不易的自由和权利的全面攻击。

sentences.en: Across our nation, we are witnessing a full-on assault on hard-fought, hard-won freedoms and rights.
sentences.zh: 她听起来确实像一个相当典型的、主流的、标准化的民主党人。

sentences.en: She really sounds like a pretty typical mainstream boilerplate Democrat.
sentences.zh: 女性对自己做出决定的自由……

sentences.en: And the freedom of a woman to make decisions about her own
sentences.zh: 她谈论堕胎。

sentences.en: She talks about abortion.
sentences.zh: 她谈论建设中产阶级。

sentences.en: She talks about building up the middle class.
sentences.zh: 一个拥有负担得起的医疗保健的未来。

sentences.en: A future with affordable health care.
sentences.zh: 她谈论我们需要如何走向未来。

sentences.en: She talks about how we need to go into the future.
sentences.zh: 我们不会走回头路。

sentences.en: We're not going to go back.
sentences.zh: 她谈论自由。

sentences.en: She talks about freedom.
sentences.zh: 我们不会走回头路，因为内华达州，我们为未来而战。

sentences.en: And we're not going back because Nevada, we fight for the future.
sentences.zh: 有些内容与她的个人经历有关，对吧？

sentences.en: Some of the stuff is linked to her biography, right?
sentences.zh: 她是检察官，但她所说的大部分内容几乎任何民主党人都可以说。

sentences.en: That she's a prosecutor, but most of what she says could be said by just about any Democrat.
sentences.zh: 所以佐治亚州，今天我问你们。
